lines.text: Researchers sent two million prompts to AI services, each hiding a fake secret.
Many apps send prompts through AI routers, which pass them along to resellers and hosting providers.
lines.title: Where your prompt travels

lines.text: Each fake secret was a canary: if anyone used it, the researcher would know who leaked it.
lines.title: The canary trick

lines.text: At least three hosting providers were broken into, and the stolen keys were used tens of thousands of times.
lines.title: What he found

lines.text: Some providers ignored privacy labels. A Zero Data Retention tag did not stop prompts from being read.
lines.title: The label vs reality

lines.text: Never paste secrets into prompts, and prefer big providers you have a direct contract with.
lines.title: Takeaways
